lessons.situation: A routine appliance repair request is waiting on landlord approval before a contractor can be chosen, and after several days the landlord has not replied, so the system flags it for manual review.
lessons.action: When the landlord approval step has gone unanswered for the set period, do not select a provider or escalate yet. Keep the job in the landlord approval stage, extend the wait, and check for a late reply from the landlord or tenant. Once a reply arrives, review it manually before moving on to provider selection.
lessons.rationale: A routine, non-urgent repair carries little risk from a short extra wait, and the landlord's approval is required before any contractor can be instructed, so the agent should wait for the reply and read it rather than act without consent.

lessons.situation: A minor maintenance request (a sticking, creaking door with misaligned hinges) is awaiting landlord approval, and after several days with no response from the landlord or tenant the system flags it for manual review.
lessons.action: Chase the landlord with a fresh, tidied-up email that restates the issue concisely without the tenant's personal availability details, offers to send a contractor to fix it where possible (or quote if the work turns out to be significant) and lets the landlord say if they would rather handle it themselves. Then place the job on hold with the reason 'Waiting for Landlord' so it is not progressed to provider selection until they reply, and return it to auto mode once you have checked no other response is owed.
lessons.rationale: Without landlord approval the job cannot move forward, so a clear, easy-to-answer chase with explicit options prompts a decision, while the hold prevents repeated automated escalations in the meantime.

lessons.situation: A tenant asked for garden clearance, levelling and gravelling, the landlord did not respond within the chase window, and the automated process flagged the job for manual review.
lessons.action: When the landlord approval wait expires with no reply, hand the job to the responsible property manager, who should contact the landlord directly (phone or direct chase) to resolve it. Once a quote is obtained and approved, book the contractor. Before works are ordered, put the job on hold to request funds up front from the landlord to cover the invoice, and keep it on hold while waiting for the provider's start date.
lessons.rationale: Escalating a stalled approval to a named person gets a decision faster than repeated automated chasing, and securing landlord funds before works begin avoids unpaid contractor invoices.

lessons.situation: A tenant promised to finish a tenant-responsible garden tidy-up and send photos the next morning, but the agency heard nothing further after several email chasers and a hold waiting on the tenant.
lessons.action: When a tenant misses a promised photo or completion deadline after written chasers, resend the request by email once more and also phone the tenant to confirm they are receiving the emails, agreeing to resend and on an alternative way to send the photos if emails still fail, then keep the job on hold awaiting the tenant's evidence.
lessons.rationale: Repeated emails with no reply may mean messages are not being delivered or seen, so a phone call quickly resolves the communication problem and gets the completion evidence needed to close the job.

lessons.situation: A confirmed repair visit has taken place, but the agency has received no work results or completion report from the contractor, so the operator has to find out what happened.
lessons.action: Phone the maintenance provider directly to ask for the job status instead of waiting for a written update. Confirm the work was completed, how any new keys will be handed over, and how the invoice will be sent, reminding them to quote the job ID in email replies. Then move the task to Result, mark the request completed, and start the final checks.
lessons.rationale: A direct call settles the missing completion information quickly and also sets out the invoicing and key-handover steps needed to close the job cleanly.

input.summary: Annual gas safety check (CP12) at 22 Alder Way expires 19 October 2026; approval needed to book a Gas Safe registered engineer, estimated £85.
input.message:
Calling Mr Dunmore, landlord of 22 Alder Way, Oldacre, ZZ2 4ZZ, job reference R/15, on 07700 900123 (number on file).
- The gas safety certificate (CP12) for the property expires on 19 October 2026, nine days from today. The annual gas safety check is a legal requirement for a let property and the property is tenanted.
- We emailed on 22 September and 2 October asking for approval and have had no reply, so we are calling.
- Proposal: book a Gas Safe registered engineer to carry out the annual gas safety check and issue a new certificate. Estimated cost £85.
- The tenant has said she is home most afternoons, so access should be straightforward.
- Ask: does Mr Dunmore approve the gas safety check at about £85? Record APPROVE or DECLINE. If he wants to use his own engineer, record the engineer's name and confirm the check will be done and the certificate sent to us before 19 October.
- Also ask whether he holds copies of earlier gas safety certificates for the property, as the tenant says she has not received one. Do not commit to any date or extra cost.

input.subject: Gas safety check – 22 Alder Way (ref R/15)
input.body:
Dear Ms Shah,

Thank you for your email about the gas certificate at 22 Alder Way, Oldacre, ZZ2 4ZZ (ref R/15).

The annual gas safety check is due before 19 October. We are getting the landlord's go-ahead so we can book a Gas Safe registered engineer, and we have noted that you are home most afternoons. We will contact you to agree a time once the engineer is arranged. We'll update you by 13 October at the latest. A copy of the new certificate will be sent to you after the check. We are also looking into the earlier certificates you mentioned.

In the meantime, if you ever smell gas: turn off the gas at the meter if it's safe to do so, open the windows, don't use switches or naked flames, leave the property and call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

Kind regards,
Donna
Maintenance team
